title: The while loop: repeating while a condition is true

visuals.title: Loop Lab: the while loop (the check comes first)

stages.name: 1. Check the condition FIRST
stages.detail: The computer asks: is the condition true right now? This happens before the body, every single time.

stages.name: 2. If false: leave
stages.detail: If it is false at the very first check, the body never runs (zero iterations). The program jumps past the loop.

stages.name: 4. Update inside the body
stages.detail: Something in the body MUST move the loop toward false: i++, num /= 10, or reading a new input. If not, the loop never ends.

stages.name: 5. Back to step 1
stages.detail: After the body, go back and check the condition again with the new values.

goal: After this you can write a while loop when you do not know in advance how many times to repeat, read input until a stop value, work with digits of a number, and spot an infinite loop.
warmup: A cashier at the canteen keeps taking items from your tray until the tray is empty. She does not know in advance whether you bought two items or ten. She just asks the same question again and again: 'Is there anything left on the tray?' While the answer is yes, she scans one more item. Another example: you keep adding mobile load until your balance reaches Rs 100. The number of rounds depends on the data, not on a fixed count.
definition: A while loop repeats its body as long as its condition is true. The condition is checked BEFORE every round, so the loop is called a pre-test (entry-controlled) loop, and the body can run zero times. Use while when the number of repetitions is not known in advance and depends on data, such as input from the user or the digits left in a number.
howItWorks: Follow the pipeline. The check comes first. If the condition is true the body runs, then the program checks again. Unlike a for loop, a while loop has no built-in update. You must put the initialisation BEFORE the loop (int i = 1;) and the update INSIDE the body (i++). If you forget the update the condition never becomes false and the loop runs forever. This is an infinite loop. In a console, press Ctrl + C to stop it. Two classic uses: (1) a sentinel loop: read a number, and keep processing until the user types a special value like -1 (the sentinel). Read once before the loop and read again at the end of the body. (2) digits: num % 10 gives the last digit and num /= 10 removes it, so while (num > 0) visits every digit.

worked.problem: Read marks until the user types -1. Then print the average of the marks entered (if at least one mark was entered).
pseudocode: IF count > 0 THEN PRINT total / count
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B["total = 0, count = 0"]
  B --> C[/Read marks/]
  C --> D{marks != -1?}
  D -->|Yes| E["total += marks, count++"]
  E --> F[/Read marks/]
  F --> D
  D -->|No| G{count > 0?}
  G -->|Yes| H[/Print average/]
  G -->|No| I([End])
  H --> I

sample.title: Average until -1 (sentinel)

explanation.text: total adds up the marks, count counts how many marks were entered.
The FIRST value is read before the loop, so the condition has something to test.
Keep going while the user has not typed the sentinel -1.
Add the mark to the total.
Read the NEXT value at the end of the body. This is the update of the loop.
Guard: if the user typed -1 straight away, count is 0 and dividing by it would be wrong.

worked.problem: Read a positive number and print the sum of its digits. For 4825 the answer is 4 + 8 + 2 + 5 = 19.
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[/Read num/]
  B --> C[sum = 0]
  C --> D{num > 0?}
  D -->|Yes| E["sum = sum + num % 10"]
  E --> F["num = num / 10"]
  F --> D
  D -->|No| G[/Print sum/]
  G --> H([End])

sample.title: Sum of digits

explanation.text: num is the input, sum collects the digits.
While digits are left (num is above 0), repeat.
num % 10 is the last digit. Add it to sum.
Integer division by 10 drops the last digit. This is the update.
After the loop num is 0 and sum holds the answer.

steps.note: num is empty, sum starts at 0.
Condition 4825 > 0 is true. Last digit 4825 % 10 = 5, so sum = 5.
Condition 482 > 0 is true. Last digit 482 % 10 = 2, so sum = 7.
Condition 48 > 0 is true. Last digit 48 % 10 = 8, so sum = 15.
Condition 4 > 0 is true. Last digit 4 % 10 = 4, so sum = 19.

variations.when: Like a for loop but the update is in the body
variations.example: int i = 1; while (i <= 5) { cout << i; i++; }

variations.when: Read until a special value such as -1 or 0
Process every digit of a number
Menu or game that stops by another rule (advanced)

mistakes.error: No compiler error. The program prints 1 forever (infinite loop) because i never changes. Press Ctrl + C to stop it.
No compiler error. The semicolon is an empty body, so the loop spins forever because i never changes.
No compiler error. marks is never read inside the loop, so the sentinel is never seen and the loop never ends.
No compiler error. Without braces only the first statement belongs to the loop, so i++ is outside and the loop is infinite.
No compiler error. Missing braces: num /= 10 runs only once after the loop, so the loop is infinite.

examTips: A while loop needs three things: initialise before, a condition, and an update inside. Check that all three are present.
Whenever you see a while loop with no change to the condition variable, write 'infinite loop'.
The body may run zero times because the condition is tested first.
For digits remember: % 10 gets the last digit, / 10 removes it, loop while num > 0.
In a sentinel loop read once before the loop and again at the end of the body.
romanSummary: while loop tab use karte hain jab pata na ho ke kitni baar repeat karna hai.
Pehle condition check hoti hai, phir body chalti hai, is liye body zero baar bhi chal sakti hai.
Initialization loop se pehle likhein aur update body ke andar, warna infinite loop ban jata hai.
Sentinel value (jaise -1) tak input lena aur digits ka sum nikalna (% 10 aur / 10) while loop ki mashhoor misalein hain.
Stuck program ko rokne ke liye Ctrl + C dabayein.

quiz.prompt: When does a while loop check its condition?
quiz.hint: It is called a pre-test loop.
quiz.explanation: The test comes first, so the body can run zero times.

quiz.prompt: What causes an infinite while loop?
quiz.explanation: If nothing in the body moves the condition toward false, the loop never ends.

quiz.prompt: What does num / 10 do to the integer 4825?
quiz.hint: Integer division drops the decimal part.
